subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Chlorine acts as a bleaching agent only in the presence of moisture – explain.

verification.note: Unit 9 (VIIA Group Elements) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book pp.86-89, the sub-box "VIIA GROUP ELEMENTS" of printed chapter 7, which prints the question and a model answer. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK GAP (book p.87, VSAQ 8): the printed answer never states the point the question turns on, that DRY chlorine has no bleaching action; it starts from the wet reaction. That sentence is written here as the first line. The printed equation Cl₂ + H₂O → 2HCl + [O] was atom-counted and balances as printed. The comparison with sulphur dioxide bleaching, which is a reduction and is temporary, is added because the two are asked together in this chapter.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Nascent oxygen from water
lines: Dry chlorine has no bleaching action.
In the presence of water, chlorine reacts
with it and sets nascent oxygen free.
[O] is nascent oxygen, the freshly formed
steps.why: Water is a reactant here, not a solvent: it supplies the oxygen. Without water there is no nascent oxygen and no bleaching, which is exactly what the question asks about. Nascent oxygen is a much stronger oxidising agent than ordinary O₂ because it is a single atom.
common_mistakes: Writing that chlorine itself removes the colour. Chlorine bleaches through the nascent oxygen made from water.
Writing O₂ in place of [O]. Ordinary oxygen gas does not bleach; the freshly formed single atom does.
steps.memory_tip: No water, no nascent oxygen, no bleaching. The water is a reactant.
steps.margin_note: The first sentence and the balanced equation together earn this mark.

steps.label: Bleaching is by oxidation
lines: The nascent oxygen oxidises the coloured
Bleaching by chlorine is an oxidation, so
Bleaching by SO₂ is a reduction and the
colour returns in air, so it is temporary.
steps.why: The oxidised coloured substance is a new compound, so the original colour does not return. Sulphur dioxide works the opposite way: it reduces the coloured substance, and the air slowly oxidises it back, so that bleaching is temporary. The two are set as a pair in this chapter.
common_mistakes: Writing that chlorine bleaching is temporary. Oxidation makes it permanent; the temporary one is SO₂.
Stopping at the equation. The word oxidation is what is being marked.
steps.memory_tip: Chlorine oxidises and the colour never returns; SO₂ reduces and the colour comes back.
steps.margin_note: Write the word oxidation and the word permanent. The equation alone is usually half this mark.

insider_note: The first line, that dry chlorine does not bleach, is the line the question is really asking for, and the printed guide leaves it out.
